From Peter Dingle, OXFORD


Dear Sir,

I have copied a program from the
INPUT magazine but it does not
save or load and run the data.
Can you please help? My main
interest is in cataloguing and
searching files for tracing your
family tree and also photograph
negative filing.

Can the other side of the Plus 3
disc be used for a demo?

             - Peter Dingle


To Peter Dingle from Brian

The program uses the same name
to save two lots of data on tape
cassette.On disc it must use two
different names. Alter line 5010
thus...
      SAVE Q$+".A" DATA A()
      SAVE Q$+".B" DATA B()

        and line 6020 thus...

      LOAD X$+".A" DATA A()
      LOAD X$+".B" DATA B()

...but you must enter a filename
of no more than 8 letters.

We may use the back of the +3
OUTLET disc for something extra
in the future. Wait and see!
                        - Brian

From Malcolm Goodman,  LEEDS



The discs I have only cost 45p
from an advertiser in COMPUTER
SHOPPER. What's the difference,
quality-wise, between these and
discs costing twice as much?

Can you advise which locations
in the system variables OUTLET
uses as flags etc. as I have a
feeling it might be possible to
store 3 different editions of
OUTLET on one disc but I need to
work out the mechanics of such
an idea first.

To Malcolm Goodman from Brian

Some cheaper discs are as good
as the more expensive - some are
inferior. There's no way to tell
but to try different suppliers.
If you get many failures, try
another source. We buy medium-
priced discs for OUTLET rather
than the cheapest as we were
getting many faults. However, we
buy ours over-the-counter at a
Leicester shop so we can get
another batch quickly. If the
discs you are using seem alright
then don't worry.

We use 23608 as the "next item"
flag. When the CONTENTS BASIC is
loaded it will load a text file
if 23608 holds between 1 and H.

If loading from the loader with
the title page then 23608 holds
CODE "LOAD" and then a jingle is
played or "press any key" or
whatever. Any other value and
the BASIC jumps straight to the
CONTENTS page.

23728 is used as the microdrive
number(removed on other versions
as some systems use 23728).

Your main problem will be
changing filenames as many are
the same from month to month.
Line 30 in the CONTENTS BASIC
holds these names and each BASIC
program loads "CONTENTS" at 8915
and the next item at 8920. Best
of British luck. At 45p a disc I
wouldn't bother mate!
                      - Brian

From Kenneth Stearn, NEWCASTLE



Dear Brian,

Please explain the line you use
to set Kempston E Interfaces,ie,
LPRINT CHR$ 27;"@";CHR$ 27;"l";
CHR$ 23; CHR$ 27;"Q 7". It's the
@, 1 and Q7 that has me stumped.


Also, is there a way of removing
the "M1 LOADING" message from
files saved using MULTIFACE 1.If
I edit and remove it,the program
will no longer load.

To Kenneth Stearn from Brian.
All computer characters have a
code number,e.g. a capital A has
the code 65. If you LPRINT a
character the computer sends the
code to the printer which
re-interprets the code as the
character and prints it. If you
send an escape code such as 27
first, however, the printer will
treat the following code as a
control code whether you LPRINT
CHR$ 65 or LPRINT "A". In fact,
there is no difference - both
commands send 65 to the printer.
The codes for @, l, Q and 7 are
64, 108, 81 and 55 respectively.
27 then 64 ("@")clears a printer
of any codes previously sent.
27,108("l"),23 sets left margin
to 23 and 27,81("Q"),55("7")sets
right margin to 55.

The only way I've found to alter
the MULTIFACE loader is to POKE
the BASIC directly but I have an
early version so yours may be
different. POKE 23845,49 first.
On mine this turns the message
blue making it invisible. If it
does not work CLEAR 65367 and
MERGE "NEXPIKA"(OUTLET 16).Enter
23755 as the start address and
study the column on the right
until you see the BASIC charact-
ers. If you see PAPER "6", POKE
the address (against 6) with 49.
The USR calls (NOT in VAL) are
phoney and should be 24795 but I
still cannot edit the line! If
experimenting note the program
cannot be loaded as a direct
command but only from a program
line or as "run".
                         - Brian

From  Steve Monk, ASHFORD, KENT

Dear Ron, Brian & readers,

Firstly I would like to wish all
OUTLET readers a happy new year.

I would like to wholly endorse
the letter from Brian Gaff in
SHOUTBURST (Issue 29). I for one
am sick to death of the contin-
ual crap the magazines pump out
month after boring month. Surely
they will run out of games soon?
What has happened to the serious
software for the Spectrum and
the excellent programmers that
used to adorn the pages of ZXC?
We could do with a GOOD spread-
sheet for the Spectrum with an
80-column print-out, good graph
drawing routines etc.

If only I could master machine
code!I have written a graphdraw-
ing program I use to draw bar
charts of my bills and I try to
beat John Snow on the telly with
the election results but I'm
sure, to you who are conversant
with m/c, it's primitive.

To add salt to the wounds,
although its early days yet, I
have had in my little hands
since December 22nd a brand new
SAM COUPE. What a machine!! If
you're a BASIC programmer, like
me, it's a dream come true. It's
fast. You can do a scrolling
message like the one used in
OUTLET all from BASIC using the
Roll command. My little graph
drawing program zips up the


screen just like a big computer
does it! [Sounds good! Why not
share your programs with other
readers via OUTLET, Steve? -BC]

Anyway, back to the point. Here
is a brilliant new 8-bit machine
with exciting new features and I
fear that it will end up a games
machine. Before receiving my Sam
I scoured the magazine racks of
the newsagents for snippets of
info. I even bought two of the
comics (Crash & SU)because they
had a snip in them on Sam but
all they seemed to be interested
in was the games aspect. I phone
up the M.G.T. hotline and I hear
something like "the following
games are Sam-compatible" - not
a word on whether Masterfile or
Tasword will run on it!

I have nothing against games or
the people that like to play
them but as Brian implies, there
is a big demand for real
programs so I hope to see in
future at least one serious
magazine dedicated to Sam and a
fresh supply of good serious
software for it .

       Best Wishes,

           Steve Monk.


I second all of that!When we get
our SAM version of OUTLET going
I hope to cram far more info in
the extra space than we can get
into the Spectrum OUTLET!
                        - Brian

how true this is? Do we really
know who there is out there
reading this? Perhaps someone
could do a survey on the
equipment still in use, or

If we believe the magazines and
all their hype then we are
surrounded by thousands of sheep
like zombies clutching their
joysticks playing the latest
"megagames". In my experience
users soon get bored with most
of the dross supplied under the
blanket term "Software".

I note there are many routines
in Outlet for Opus, Disciple and
Microdrive users. Many people
have printers and use one of the
several versions of Tasword.This
must be an indication that the
machines are used for more than
just games.


What has happened to the serious
writers?I noted that one monthly
magazine lost ALL it's serious
pages at a stroke. I haven't
bought any further issues of
that magazine.

Having said this, I only really
look at Spectrum-inclusive
magazines.

processed this letter on a
machine that cost me `80.00 with
a tv costing about `150.00 and a
`120.00'ish printer.That's quite
a bit less than the cheapest pc
setup I've come across. I store
all necessary data for a local,
non-computer organisation on
disk using the same computer.

I believe it is the media that
has produced such high interest
in those highly-overrated
machines. It is also the LACK of
proper coverage at the lower end
of the media that has done like-

wise and it is the latter which
may cause the demise of the home
computer industry.

Keep up the good work.

Speccys of the world unite!!

          - Neil Morgan

Hear, Hear! Perhaps we serious
Spectrum users didn't make
enough noise years ago for the
media to notice us which is why
I recommend we support the new
Popular Computing Weekly
Spectrum column written by Brian
Gaff. It's mostly serious stuff
and is outgrowing the PC, ST and
AMIGA columns! Great stuff! As
for CP/M - read my reply to Ian
Ramage.            - Brian

anyone else see it?

but just thrown in as a"take-it-

This material could be added to

version could be easily expanded
to a C40 or C60; The Disciple/+D
and SAM disc can already take
much more material and for the
Opus version I guess we could
offer an extra optional disc for
a small fee...
                        - Brian

From James Smith, WOKINGHAM

I am having a problem with my
new program, CLOCK. It is
interrupt-driven and uses IM2
with a vector table. The program
will happily work with addresses
C000-C003:-

     C003   C002  C001  C000
     HOURS  MINS  SECS  1/50

It correctly carries from one
address to the next, e.g. 60
seconds = 1 minute but I display
the time on-screen at position
0,23 so I need to save the
original AT position both when I
am using #2 and #0 as the
program uses interrupts. I have
tried PUSHing the contents of

23688 and 23689. I have also
tried PUSHing (IY+2),23612 but
the program crashes badly. I
RES 0,(IY+2) to make sure the
clock appears in #2. I tried
opening the output channel to #2
but Interface 1 didn't like that
so please help!

                James Smith

To James Smith from Brian

I don't think it is possible to
use the ROM printing routines to
print from an interrupt-driven
program (EI in the ROM?). Leave
the ROM alone.Use the listing on
the next page to print. I'm
hoping your program calculates
each DIGIT to be printed (i.e. 3
then 2 rather than 32). You then
call my PRINT routine with the
digit code in the A register but
before you start each pass (to
print the whole 8 characters in
e.g.15:32:07, you must put 16407
(the address of the top line of
the PRINT position at 0,23) into
SCRNAD with e.g. LD DE,16407
LD (SCRNAD),DE. Write again if
you need more help.     - Brian

       LD H,0
       LD L,A       ;Calc addr.

From Peter Smith, DOVER

Every few months a +3 disk
refuses to load giving the error
"Drive A, Track 1, Sector 0,
missing address mark". I have
D.I.C.E. version 1, but it can't
help. It gives a message "Dos
error 5, track 1.." etc.Also the
program keeps attempting to read
the directory so I have to reset
the computer with the drive
running.Doesn't this corrupt the
disk even more ? Ironically one
of these faulty disks was near
full of various file back-ups so
I have the originals.It is still
very inconvenient to remake all
these back-ups. Is there no way
that I can replace this missing
address mark?

To Peter Smith from Brian

Firstly,a thousand apologies for
misplacing your letter from last
October.

Now, if DICE cannot help then I
doubt the discs can be saved. I
recommend you try a different
brand and source of discs as you
seem to be getting a high number
of failures.After formatting,you
could also verify the disc by
filling it with code files and
reloading them with a loop,e.g.,
FOR N=1 TO 17: SAVE STR$ N CODE
0,10000:NEXT N. Repeat with LOAD
then ERASE instead of SAVE. You
might also check the discs and
equipment are not operated or
stored at low temperatures.
                        - Brian

Dear Ron,

To Kenneth Stearn from Brian. All computer characters have a code number,e.g. a capital A has the code 65. If you LPRINT a character the computer sends the code to the printer which re-interprets the code as the character and prints it. If you send an escape code such as 27 first, however, the printer will treat the following code as a control code whether you LPRINT CHR$ 65 or LPRINT "A". In fact, there is no difference - both commands send 65 to the printer. The codes for @, l, Q and 7 are 64, 108, 81 and 55 respectively. 27 then 64 ("@")clears a printer of any codes previously sent. 27,108("l"),23 sets left margin to 23 and 27,81("Q"),55("7")sets right margin to 55.

The only way I've found to alter the MULTIFACE loader is to POKE the BASIC directly but I have an early version so yours may be different. POKE 23845,49 first. On mine this turns the message blue making it invisible. If it does not work CLEAR 65367 and MERGE "NEXPIKA"(OUTLET 16).Enter 23755 as the start address and study the column on the right until you see the BASIC charact- ers. Kenneth Stearn от Brian:
Все компьютерные символы имеют свой код, например, заглавная «A» имеет код 65. Если вы делаете LPRINT символа, компьютер отправляет этот код на принтер, который интерпретирует код как символ и печатает его. Однако, если вы сначала отправляете escape-код, например 27, принтер воспримет следующий код как управляющий — независимо от того, напишете ли вы `LPRINT CHR$ 65` или `LPRINT "A"`. На самом деле разницы нет — обе команды отправляют на принтер число 65. Коды для `@`, `l`, `Q` и `7` — это соответственно 64, 108, 81 и 55.

27, а затем 64 (`"@"`) сбрасывает принтер от любых ранее отправленных команд.
27, 108 (`"l"`), 23 устанавливает левое поле на 23, а 27, 81 (`"Q"`), 55 (`"7"`) устанавливает правое поле на 55.

Единственный найденный мной способ изменить загрузчик MULTIFACE — это напрямую делать POKE в Бейсик, но у меня ранняя версия, так что ваша может отличаться. Сначала сделайте `POKE 23845,49`. На моем компьютере это делает сообщение синим, то есть невидимым. Если это не сработает, сделайте `CLEAR 65367` и `MERGE "NEXPIKA"` (OUTLET 16). Введите 23755 в качестве начального адреса и изучайте правый столбец, пока не увидите символы Бейсика. Если увидите `PAPER "6"`, сделайте POKE по этому адресу (напротив 6) значением 49. Вызовы USR (НЕ в VAL) фиктивные и должны быть 24795, но отредактировать строку я все равно не могу! Экспериментируя, учтите, что программу нельзя загрузить прямой командой — только из строки программы или через «run».
— Brian
